## Free draft (free_draft.md): status of every claim
Free draft (free_draft.md): 25 claims: 0 verified (VP), 25 unverified (memory), 0 removed; every item of the draft taken up in this card is verified or carries the mark "unverified (memory)".
Free phase: 25 distinct leads and 7 quantified orders of magnitude kept from 25 claims; 0% of the claims verified (other leads remain marked "unverified (memory)").
- D1 [unverified (memory)] Compare felt sleeves and folded paper cradles for protecting painted wooden tiles; the inspection rubric records face scratches separately from corner chips and every material label is masked.
- D2 [unverified (memory)] The invented North bench uses square tiles with rounded painted corners; square blanks receive identical paint coats and dry on separate racks before the packing assignments are shuffled.
- D3 [unverified (memory)] The invented East bench uses rectangular tiles with rough wooden edges; rectangular blanks are numbered on their backs and their original edge roughness is recorded before they enter a tray.
- D4 [unverified (memory)] A soft liner might prevent scuffs without changing the packing order; volunteers use a fixed sleeve overlap and a cardboard gauge so that material softness is not confounded with fit.
- D5 [unverified (memory)] A stiff cradle might restrain sliding while leaving the corners exposed; the paper fold angle is fixed with a wooden jig and repeated measurements record how much the tile slides.
- D6 [unverified (memory)] The synthetic padded-cradle source reports fewer marks on the corner panels; the synthetic source describes padded corners under a single loading condition and leaves washing durability unresolved.
- D7 [unverified (memory)] The synthetic paper-only source leaves the sleeve contribution unresolved; the paper-only control uses the same volunteer and the same inspection lamp but receives no removable felt insert.
- D8 [unverified (memory)] Packing order could account for an apparent difference between materials; the two materials alternate between benches so that fatigue and practice cannot remain tied to one packing assignment.
- D9 [unverified (memory)] Bench humidity could change how the felt sleeve grips a painted tile; humidity is recorded for each bench and the primary contrast is paired within the same handling session.
- D10 [unverified (memory)] Repeated handling might wear out the sleeve before the cradle loses stiffness; washing cycles are assigned before inspection and the thickness of each reused sleeve is measured with the same gauge.
- D11 [unverified (memory)] A hidden inspection label could influence a volunteer counting surface marks; the inspection label is covered with an opaque patch and the order of photographs is independently shuffled.
- D12 [unverified (memory)] The fictional cupboard holds 32 000 wooden tile blanks for practice batches; storage bins separate unpainted blanks from confirmation tiles and no inventory count is treated as measured evidence.
- D13 [unverified (memory)] A practice tray holds 12 painted tiles separated by removable paper walls; each removable wall is cut from the same paper stock and volunteers leave an equal clearance around the painted edges.
- D14 [unverified (memory)] The synthetic drawer catalogue lists 4 000 reusable felt sleeves in storage; the synthetic catalogue is a made-up inventory and its sleeve count does not establish how long a sleeve will remain useful.
- D15 [unverified (memory)] An invented pilot assumes that roughly sixty tiles can be inspected per hour; the assumed inspection speed is an order of magnitude for planning and must be checked on a separate masked pilot batch.
- D16 [unverified (memory)] Use matching tile pairs to compare the sleeve with the paper cradle alone; matching uses size and initial surface condition only and no later scuff score is available when pairs are formed.
- D17 [unverified (memory)] The fictional workshop stores more than 32 000 wooden tile blanks, about 3 million paper squares, and 175 million tiny inspection stickers.
- D18 [unverified (memory)] A synthetic sleeve batch reaches 4 000 pieces within 75 days, while fewer than 2 percent of trial sleeves are discarded; the invented production schedule tests a spaced thousands separator and does not justify any claim about packing efficiency.
- D19 [unverified (memory)] Observe 7 packing sessions and inspect the tiles after 15 sessions; a simple scuff check uses 140 tiles but comparing two sleeve patterns needs around 280 tile pairs; the planned contrast keeps the pilot separate and reads the confirmation batches only after the comparison rule is frozen.
- D20 [unverified (memory)] Photograph each tile under the same lamp before a masked inspection; photographing tiles from the same angle prevents lamp glare from being mistaken for a difference between packing materials.
- D21 [unverified (memory)] Reserve later packing sessions to check whether the sleeve effect persists; the later session uses fresh painted tiles and retains the original sleeve dimensions rather than retuning them after seeing damage.
- D22 [unverified (memory)] Test an empty cradle as a negative control for changes in handling order.
- D23 [unverified (memory)] Add a rough insert to a separate control tray to check inspection sensitivity; the rough insert should create an obvious mark without occupying a slot in the primary paired comparison.
- D24 [unverified (memory)] Compare circular and square tile shapes as neighbouring packing experiments.
- D25 [unverified (memory)] The durability of the invented sleeve material remains unknown after repeated washing; uncertain washing durability and paint transfer are reasons to inspect reused sleeves before making a workshop recommendation.

## Critique of the protocol: claude via subagent
Test revision: not recorded [REVISION]; detail: IDEA-REPORT.md
Critique: same family (no independent critic available)
Synthetic packing case 109: compare felt sleeves and paper cradles using independent tile inspections.
Items: 7 (1 claimed fixed, not proven, 6 open); a correction counts as fixed only with a proof and the confirmation of the second critique.
- [blocking] T3 false_discrimination: The third packing trial cannot discriminate sleeve protection from the handling rival: the null stop frequency is only 66.3 percent. -> open: Synthetic packing case 111: compare felt sleeves and paper cradles using independent tile inspections.
- [major] T1 trap_unaddressed: The intact-tile target includes the corner marks already used to choose the sleeve material, leaving target circularity. -> open: Synthetic packing case 113: compare felt sleeves and paper cradles using independent tile inspections.
- [major] T1 leakage: The main packing interval includes pilot sessions used to select sleeve thickness, so design and confirmation are mixed. -> open: Synthetic packing case 115: compare felt sleeves and paper cradles using independent tile inspections.
- [major] T1 underpowered: The simulated sleeve effect 0.15 exceeds the minimum useful change 0.11; power at the useful change is inadequate under shared bench conditions. -> open: Synthetic packing case 117: compare felt sleeves and paper cradles using independent tile inspections.
- [major] all decision_rule_loophole: The revise branch is nested inside continue and allows extra packing sessions without a fixed limit. -> open: Synthetic packing case 119: compare felt sleeves and paper cradles using independent tile inspections.
- [major] T2 false_discrimination: The second trial must compare sleeve advantages between inspection sheets, rather than absolute intact-tile proportions. -> claimed fixed, not proven: Synthetic packing case 121: compare felt sleeves and paper cradles using independent tile inspections.
- [major] T3 trap_unaddressed: Known damaged tiles must be inspected separately from the primary tray to avoid contaminating the intact-tile count. -> open: Synthetic packing case 125: compare felt sleeves and paper cradles using independent tile inspections.
- Critic trap verdicts (4 traps per test): T2 1 addressed, 3 unclear; T1 1 addressed, 2 not_addressed, 1 unclear; T3 2 addressed, 1 not_addressed, 1 unclear
